question: Under Article 8c of the Schengen Borders Code, children under 12 years of age cannot use automated border control systems. The Commission’s Practical Handbook for Border Guards states that Member States using such systems should maintain sufficient non-automated lanes for children and persons accompanying them.

A constituent of mine, an Irish citizen who recently travelled with a child through both Paris Charles de Gaulle and Rome Fiumicino airports, has informed me that when they were unable to use the automated gates, they were instead directed to an ’all passports’ queue. On both occasions, this resulted in a wait of over 90 minutes, while other EU citizens passed through the automated gates.
Article 10 of the Schengen Borders Code provides that persons enjoying free movement rights under EU law are entitled to use lanes designated ‘EU, EEA, CH’. In this context: 1.

Does the Commission consider that directing EU citizens travelling with children to ‘all passports’ queues, without adequate access to staffed EU/EEA/CH lanes, is consistent with the Schengen Borders Code?

Will the Commission consider further guidance to ensure that EU families with children under 12 years of age do not face disproportionate waiting times because they cannot use automated border control systems?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (24.11.2026) According to Article 10(2) of the Schengen Borders Code1, persons enjoying the right of free movement under EU law are entitled to use the EU lanes indicated in its Annex III.

Article 10(4) allows to exceptionally suspend the rules on the use of different lanes at specific border crossing points, in the event of temporary imbalance in traffic flow, for the time necessary to eliminate such imbalance. As a result, EU citizens, including EU families with children, shall normally be allowed to use the EU lanes at external air border crossing points.

The use of e-gates is a different matter, primarily regulated by national law. Article 8(c) of the Schengen Borders Code allows Member States to create e-gates but prescribes that their use is never possible for children under 12 years. The reason for this restriction is that fingerprints and facial images of children change fast as they grow.

This may indeed lead to a situation, under which EU families with children may be excluded from using e-gates and may be requested to use a ‘normal’ (not automated) EU lane. According to Article 15 of the Schengen Borders Code, Member States shall deploy appropriate staff and resources in sufficient numbers to ensure an efficient, high and uniform level of control at their external borders.

The Commission Practical Handbook for Border Guards2 sets out recommendations to Member States for reducing waiting times at external border crossing points, including the recommendation to maintain non-automated lanes in sufficient numbers for children and persons accompanying children.
1 Regulation (EU) 2016/399 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 9 March 2016 on a Union Code on
the rules governing the movement of persons across borders; ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/399/oj. 2 https://ec.europa.eu/transparency/documents-register/detail?ref=C(2022)7591&lang=en.
